Model-based clustering

Source: R/seg_cluster.R
seg_cluster_model.Rd

Fits Gaussian mixture models with mclust::Mclust() and assigns each respondent to the cluster with the highest probability. Requires the mclust package.

Usage

seg_cluster_model(
  x,
  k = 4,
  model_names = NULL,
  plots = TRUE,
  cluster_plot_args = list(),
  dend_args = list(),
  centers_args = list(),
  heatmap_n = 200,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

The output of seg_prep_data() (recommended), or a data frame or numeric matrix with already prepared clustering variables (no missing values).

k

Number of clusters (or a vector of values). NULL lets the BIC choose among 1 to 9 clusters (slow).

model_names

Covariance models to consider, e.g. c("EII", "VVV"). NULL (default) considers all models. See mclust::mclustModelNames().

plots

Logical. Whether to create the plots. Defaults to TRUE.

cluster_plot_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_cluster(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_cluster()), e.g. list(ellipse.type = "convex").

dend_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_dend(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_dend()), e.g. list(type = "phylogenic").

centers_args

A list of arguments passed to seg_plot_centers(), overriding the defaults, e.g. list(type = "bars", scale = "original").

heatmap_n

Number of respondents randomly sampled for the heatmap. Defaults to 200.

seed

Random seed. The global random seed is left untouched. Defaults to 123.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the results. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

For a single number of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster, a list with the elements:

  • method, family: the clustering method and its family.

  • k: the requested number of clusters (NA for density-based methods).

  • k_found: the number of clusters found (excluding noise).

  • cluster: integer vector with the cluster of each respondent (0 = noise), in the order of the prepared data.

  • membership: matrix with the membership degrees (fuzzy) or probabilities (model-based) of each respondent in each cluster, NULL for the other methods.

  • sizes: tibble with the size and share of each cluster.

  • centers: tibble with the mean of each clustering variable per cluster.

  • assignment: tibble with the respondent identifier, the cluster and method-specific information (e.g. the highest membership degree).

  • data, data_full, dist: the prepared clustering variables, the original data of the retained respondents and the distance matrix (if available), as passed on from seg_prep_data().

  • fit: the result of the underlying clustering function.

  • tree: the hierarchical tree (class hclust) for hierarchical methods and hierarchical k-means, otherwise NULL.

  • cluster_map: named integer vector mapping the cluster codes of fit (names) to the renumbered codes, NULL if not renumbered.

  • prep: the preparation settings of seg_prep_data() (variables, missing values, rescaling parameters), used to prepare new respondents in predict.seg_cluster().

  • plots: list of plots (see "Visualizations").

  • settings: list of the settings used.

For several numbers of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster_set, a list with the elements solutions (named list of seg_cluster objects, e.g. solutions$k4), summary (tibble with the cluster sizes per solution), plot (the cluster plots of all solutions combined) and method.

Details

Algorithm

Model-based clustering assumes that the data comes from a mixture of k groups, each following a multivariate normal distribution with its own mean and covariance matrix. The covariance matrix determines the shape, volume and orientation of each cluster (ellipsoids). mclust offers 14 models, from simple (e.g. "EII": spherical clusters of equal volume) to flexible (e.g. "VVV": ellipsoids of varying shape, volume and orientation).

  1. For each model and number of clusters, the parameters are estimated with the EM algorithm (expectation-maximization), starting from a hierarchical clustering: the E-step computes the probability of each respondent to belong to each cluster, the M-step updates the means and covariances based on these probabilities.

  2. The models are compared with the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), which balances fit and complexity; the model with the highest BIC is selected (plots$bic).

Each respondent is assigned to the cluster with the highest probability (cluster); the probabilities are returned in membership, and the uncertainty of the assignment (1 minus the highest probability) in assignment$uncertainty.

Number of clusters

With k = NULL, the BIC chooses the number of clusters among 1 to 9 as well. This is statistically principled, but slow (about one minute for 1,400 respondents and 20 variables) and, in large samples, the BIC tends to favor many clusters. With a given k (or a vector of values), the best model is chosen for each k.

When to use

When clusters of different shapes and sizes are expected, membership probabilities are needed, or the number of clusters should be chosen on statistical grounds. Model-based clustering can produce very unequal cluster sizes, and with many variables the flexible models have many parameters to estimate. It uses the data (not the distance matrix).

See also

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  prep <- seg_prep_data(
    sm_synthetic,
    vars = dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"),
    missing = "mice",
    max_missing_prop = 0.2,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  mc <- seg_cluster_model(prep, k = 4)
  mc$plots$bic
}
#> 
#> ── Cluster solution: Model-based clustering (VVE), k = 4 ──
#> 
#> • Cluster 1: n = 648 (47%)
#> • Cluster 2: n = 480 (35%)
#> • Cluster 3: n = 203 (15%)
#> • Cluster 4: n = 40 (3%)
#> Plots: `$plots$cluster`, `$plots$heatmap`, `$plots$centers`, and `$plots$bic`

# }
